strings.name: Tim Cook
strings.role: Apple executive chair · Supply chains and consumer technology
strings.summary: Cook began in industrial engineering and operations, joining Apple in 1998 before succeeding Steve Jobs as CEO. During his leadership, Apple expanded wearables, services and products using its own chips while developing global supply-chain management. In September 2026 he became executive chair, with John Ternus succeeding him as CEO.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through November 13, 2026. Apple’s official leadership page confirms the September 2026 transition; Cook is no longer described as current CEO. His birthplace is given only as Alabama because sources differ on the city.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Bachelor’s in industrial engineering, Auburn University (1982); MBA, Duke University (1988)
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Associated organizations
strings.facts.fact-03.value: Apple; previously IBM, Intelligent Electronics and Compaq
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Global operations and supply chains
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Rose through Apple’s operations leadership, managing global supply chains, sales and service systems.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Expanding products and services
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: As CEO, oversaw new product categories including Apple Watch and the expansion of services.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: The Mac chip transition
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: During his leadership Apple introduced M1 Macs, beginning the shift from Intel processors to Apple silicon.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Becomes Apple executive chair
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Concluded his CEO tenure and became executive chair; John Ternus succeeded him as chief executive.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Elected to the National Academy of Engineering
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Auburn University announced his election to the US National Academy of Engineering’s class of 2026.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Introduces the first M1 Macs
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Apple unveiled MacBook Air, 13-inch MacBook Pro and Mac mini models using its own M1 chip.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Unveils Apple Watch
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Apple announced the first Apple Watch, expanding into a new wearable-device category.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Succeeds Jobs as Apple CEO
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The board appointed him chief executive after Steve Jobs resigned.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes chief operating officer
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took charge of worldwide sales and operations, continuing to coordinate supply chains and support services.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Joins Apple
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became senior vice president of operations, advancing the company’s operations and supply-chain management.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Earns a Duke MBA
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Completed a master’s in business administration and was named a Fuqua Scholar.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Graduates from Auburn
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Earned a bachelor’s in industrial engineering and then began working at IBM.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Alabama
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born and raised in Alabama, later attending Auburn University.
